sources.quote: Chemical composition of the conventional cold-rolled SS316L and spherical SS316L powders.

The fabricated SLM samples were subjected to two different heat treatments: a typical furnace-type heat treatment conducted at 1100 °C for 0.5 h and hot isostatic pressing performed at 1100 °C and 100 MPa for 1.5 h.
The building chamber ... was maintained at an oxygen concentration below 0.5 vol% ... filled with argon gas (purity: 99.99%) to prevent oxidation.

The experimental conditions for the SLM process were fixed at a layer thickness of 0.03 mm and a hatch distance of 0.12 mm. The laser power ranged from 100 to 140 W, and the laser beam scan speed varied from 100 to 280 mm/s.
The laser beam scanned the layer with a chessboard strategy ... blocks with dimensions of 5 × 5 mm2 ... adjacent blocks ... 90° ... every chessboard scan direction was rotated by 30°.
Experimental conditions and measured density for the SLM SS316L samples. Typical furnace-type of HT and HIP were conducted after the SLM process.

The tensile strength was measured ... at a crosshead speed of 0.005 mm/s. The sample geometry and testing parameters followed ... ASTM E8/E8M–16a ... microhardness ... load of 200 kgf and a holding time of 10 s.
A dry sliding wear test was conducted ... following the requirements of ASTM G99 ... total sliding distance was 200 m with a sliding speed of 28.8 mm/s and a normal load of 30 N.
The SLM samples were fabricated at a laser power of 120 W and scan speed of 100 mm/s ... as-SLM ... 99.5 MPa ... HT-SLM ... 17.8 MPa ... HIP-SLM ... 27.5 MPa.
The number and size of pores decreased with increasing laser power and decreasing scan speed ... high density ... increasing the laser energy density.
as-SLM grain size 17.6 μm; HT-SLM 21.4 μm; HIP-SLM 22.9 μm; cellular microstructure disappeared after heat treatment.
Mechanical properties of CR and SLM samples: hardness, yield strength, tensile strength, elongation.
Heat treatments decreased hardness/tensile strength and improved elongation; dimples and pores were observed on fracture surfaces.

The yield strengths and elongation were measured as 464.8 MPa and 32.8%, as well as 222.5 MPa and 63.5% for the as-SLM and CR, respectively. After the heat treatments of the as-SLM, the elongation significantly improved to 48.2 and 51.3% for the HT-SLM and HIP-SLM, respectively.
For the as-SLM(120/100), the COF was found to be 0.54; however, the HT-SLM(120/100) and HIP-SLM(120/100) samples ... 0.62 and 0.63, respectively.

Comparable wear loss was obtained for the CR (0.56 mm3) and as-SLM(120/100) (0.57 mm3) ... heat treatments deteriorated the wear resistance ... wear loss was found to be 0.57 and 0.67 mm3 for as-SLM(120/100) and as-SLM(120/280), respectively.
Pores and accumulated wear debris were observed in the contact area of the as-SLM samples after the pin-on-disk test.
The heat treatments induced a decrease in the tensile strength, as well as an increase in the elongation ... heat treatments deteriorated wear resistance.
